title: `truncated` flag is a false positive when exactly max_examples distinct invalid values exist
description: The error context computes `truncated=len(invalid_values) >= max_examples`. But `invalid_values` is produced by `.head(max_examples)`, so `len(invalid_values)` can never exceed `max_examples`; the comparison is true precisely when `len == max_examples`. That condition is reached both when the invalid set was genuinely larger than `max_examples` (truly truncated) AND when there were exactly `max_examples` distinct invalid values with none dropped. In the latter case `truncated=True` is wrong and would mislead an operator/log consumer into believing more invalid levels exist than were reported. The standard fix is to materialise `max_examples + 1` examples and report `truncated = len(examples) > max_examples` (then trim for display).
evidence: Line 456-461 builds `... .head(max_examples) .implode()`. Line 469-473 yields at most `max_examples` items. Line 481 sets `truncated=len(invalid_values) >= max_examples`, so a column with exactly `max_examples` distinct out-of-domain values reports `truncated=True` despite the list being complete.
